THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 482 OF CR.P.C. PRAYING TO QUASH THE ENTIRE FIR REGISTERED IN CR.NO.41/2022 REGISTERED BY THE 1ST RESPONDENT i.e,
RAJAJINAGAR POLICE, BENGALURU FOR THE ALLEGED OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTIONS 323, 504, 506,
498A READ WITH SECTION 34 OF IPC AND SECTIONS 3 AND 4 OF DOWRY PROHIBITION ACT ON THE FILE OF XXXIX ADDL.C.M.M., BENGALURU IN SO FAR AS THE PETITIONERS ARE CONCERNED HEREIN.

THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA  COMMON ORAL ORDER

The petitioner in Crl.P.No.11199/2022 being the husband of respondent No.2, arrayed as accused No.1 and the NC: 2024:KHC:45679 petitioners in Crl.P.No.5606/2022 being the mother-in-law and brother-in-law of respondent No.2, arrayed as accused Nos.2 and 3 in Crime No.41/2022 of Rajajinagar Police Station, pending in C.C.No.22965/2022 on the file of the learned XXXIX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Bangalore, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 504, 506, 498A read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code ( for short 'IPC') and Sections 3 and 4 of The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (for short 'DP Act') are seeking to quash the criminal proceedings pending against them.
2. Brief facts of the case are that, respondent No.2 filed the first information against accused Nos. 1 to 3 alleging commission of offences as stated above.
It is her specific contention that she married accused No.1 on 03.10.2019.
The accused demanded and accepted dowry in the form of cash, gold ornaments, suit etc.,
After marriage, she started residing in her matrimonial house with the accused.
The accused were ill-treating her for silly reasons and they were also demanding additional dowry.
She gave birth to a girl child on 23.07.2020 and since then, she was residing in her parental house.
Accused No.1 has not given anything towards the maintenance NC: 2024:KHC:45679 of respondent No.2 and her child.
It is alleged that the petitioners were abusing respondent No.2 for not giving birth to the male child.

It is also alleged that on 16.11.2020, the accused came to the parental house Smt. Lakshmamma vs State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195248343/
3 of respondent No.2 and picked up quarrel with her.

sentences.text: On 17.11.2020, accused No.1 had assaulted the father and brother-in-law of respondent No.2.
On 04.04.2021, the accused have illegally trespassed into her parental house and abused her in filthy language and assaulted the sister and brother-in-law of respondent No.2.
In that regard, NCR No.63/2021 was registered.

3. It is stated by the informant that on 01.08.2021, accused No.1 suddenly trespassed into her parental house, locked the door and threatened her to write on a paper that she is giving divorce to him and that she is not seeking any maintenance either for herself or for her child.
Accordingly, she signed the blank papers.
It is stated that accused No.1 criminally intimidated the informant not to reveal this fact to anybody else or to face dire consequences.
4. It is stated that, by misusing the signature of the informant on blank paper, the legal notice was sent on NC: 2024:KHC:45679 04.08.2021, making baseless allegations.
Rowdies were sent near the house of the informant.
Therefore, she requested the police to register the case and to take legal action.
Accordingly, the police have registered the case and took up investigation.
Hence, the petitioners are before this Court seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them.

5. Heard Sri Shivaraj N Arali, learned counsel for the petitioner in Crl.P.No.11199/2022, Sri Gowthamdev C Ullal, learned counsel for the petitioners in Crl.P.No. 5606/2022 and Smt. Rashmi Jadhav, learned Additional SPP for respondent No.1.
Perused the materials on records.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner in Crl.P.No.11199/2022 is accused No.1 - the husband of respondent No.2 and the petitioners in Crl.P.No.5606/2022 are accused Nos. 2 and 3 - mother and brother of accused No.1.
The marriage of accused No.1 with respondent No.2 was solemnized on 03.10.2019.
Respondent No.2 who had gone to her parental house for delivery had not returned back.
Initially, a complaint was filed on 06.04.2021, alleging that the accused are asking her to return to the NC: 2024:KHC:45679 matrimonial house.
It is also alleged that accused No.1 assaulted the informant, her sister and brother-in-law, abused them in filthy language and demanded gold chain for the child and insisted to get a male child.
There was a mediation and accordingly, the informant had withdrawn the complaint stating that, she is not ready to come to her matrimonial house, rather she opted to stay back in her parental house.
Even after several months, she has not returned to her matrimonial house and therefore, legal notice was sent on 04.08.2021, seeking Restitution of Conjugal Rights.
Reply was issued on 18.09.2021 making all sorts of allegations.
The rejoinder was issued to accused No.1 denying the allegations made by the informant and also specifically stating as to how the allegations are false.
Thereafter, accused No.1 filed the complaint dated 29.03.2022 against the sister of the informant and her husband asking them to send his wife and child to his house.
As a counter blast, the present complaint came to be filed.
There is inordinate delay in filing the complaint and baseless allegations are made without any basis.
Even though, the charge sheet is filed, there are absolutely no materials to substantiate the contentions.
The history narrated above discloses that NC: 2024:KHC:45679 deliberately false allegations were made and to the complaint was filed.
It is a clear case of abuse of process of Court and hence, prays for allowing the petition.

Learned counsel for the petitioners in Crl.P.No.5606/2022 adopted the contentions taken by the learned counsel for the petitioner in Crl.P.No.11199/2022.
8.
Per contra, learned Additional SPP opposing the petitions submits that serious allegations are made by the informant against all the three accused.
After investigation, the charge sheet is filed.
Looking to the nature and seriousness of the allegations, the petitioners are not entitled for any relief. Accordingly, she prays for dismissal of the petitions.

9. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the Petitioners have made out any grounds to allow the petitions and to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them?"
NC: 2024:KHC:45679 My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 10.
The facts narrated by the learned counsel for the petitioner in Crl.P.No.11199/2022 as stated above is not controverted.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the petitioner has produced the first complaint dated 06.04.2021 filed by the informant against accused No.1 specifically stating that, she has delivered the child about 8 months back and she is residing in her parental house.
Subsequently, the informant withdrawn the complaint subject to condition that she prefers to stay back in her parental house and will not return to her matrimonial house.
11. On 04.08.2021, accused No.1 issued the legal notice seeking restitution of conjugal rights and a reply dated 18.09.2021 was issued by the informant, making allegations against the accused.
It is alleged that they have demanded and accepted dowry, ill-treated her, threatened and assaulted her etc.,
The rejoinder dated 02.09.2021 was issued by accused No.1 denying all those allegations.
However, neither the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:45679 informant has initiated any action with regard to those allegations nor the accused has sought for restitution of conjugal rights.
But on the other hand, accused No.1 filed the complaint against sister and brother-in-law of the informant on 29.03.2020 asking them to advice his wife and send her to the matrimonial house.
This must have triggered the informant and her family members, as a result of which, the present complaint came to be filed on 05.04.2022.
Even though several allegations were made against the accused, it was only on 05.04.2022, even though the date of marriage is 03.10.2019 and the reply notice was sent on 18.09.2021.
There is absolutely no reason for the inordinate delay in filing the complaint.
It is not made clear as to why the informant waited for years to file the criminal complaint.
There are no reasons for withdrawing the first complaint.
It is also not explained as to why no such allegations were made while filing the first complaint.

In view of all these facts and circumstances, I am of the opinion that it is not a fit case for Smt. Lakshmamma vs State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195248343/
5 trial.

Therefore, I am of the opinion that the criminal proceeding is liable to be quashed.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the Affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The petitions are allowed.

(ii) The FIR registered in Crime No.41/2022 of Rajajinagar Police Station, pending in C.C.No.22965/2022 on the file of the learned XXXIX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Bangalore, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 504, 506, 498A read with Section 34 of 'IPC' and Sections 3 and 4 of 'DP Act') is hereby quashed.
